discovery.model: Linear one-dimensional single-spatial-Fourier-mode electrons, fixed ions.
discovery.geometry: One velocity coordinate and one spatial Fourier mode.
discovery.boundary: One-dimensional finite velocity grid; Fn selects fixed equilibria; Fn=3 returns +1 on (-1,0), -1 on (0,1), and 0 outside that support, with 0 at v=-1,0,1; weak Fn4 cutoff requires a uniform grid; no time evolution.

identity.relation: g=f0_prime for the selected equilibrium; Fn=3 is the piecewise triangle derivative and Fn=4 includes A/(|v|^3+vt^3) cutoff jump masses.
identity.definition: g=f0_prime. For Fn=3, f0=max(0,1-|v|) and g=+1 on (-1,0), g=-1 on (0,1), and g=0 at v=-1,0,1 and outside [-1,1]. For Fn=4, g includes A/(|v|^3+vt^3) cutoff jump masses.

identity.geometry: One velocity coordinate and one spatial Fourier mode.
identity.boundary: One-dimensional finite velocity grid; Fn selects fixed equilibria; Fn=3 returns +1 on (-1,0), -1 on (0,1), and 0 outside that support, with 0 at v=-1,0,1; weak Fn4 cutoff requires a uniform grid; no time evolution.
assumptions: Velocity-window truncation and recurrence are separate from temporal integration error.

inputs.name: vv
inputs.constraints: Finite one-dimensional; aligned with df and df0dv when applicable.

inputs.name: Fn
inputs.description: Built-in equilibrium, unit density: 1 Maxwellian exp(-v^2/2)/sqrt(2pi) (unit variance); 2 kappa Gamma(kappa)/(Gamma(kappa-1/2) sqrt(2 pi kappa)) (1+v^2/(2 kappa))^-kappa, i.e. theta^2=2 with variance 2kappa/(2kappa-3), NOT unit temperature; 3 triangle max(0,1-|v|), whose returned derivative is zero outside its support; 4 cutoff slowing-down.

inputs.name: k
inputs.description: Spatial Fourier wavenumber in inverse Debye length.

inputs.name: kappa
inputs.description: Kappa index of the Fn=2 family. The family is not rescaled to unit variance; for a kappa distribution at a prescribed temperature pass its derivative as df0dv to vp_init.

inputs.name: cutoff_mode
inputs.description: Fn4 weak derivative or explicit source smooth-only forcing.
inputs.constraints: weak or smooth; weak Fn4 requires increasing uniform grid.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Tuple (g,wr,wi): g [N], theoretical wr=1 and wi=-k sqrt(2) only for Fn=2,kappa=1; otherwise theory is None. Returns a tuple positionally: the caller unpacks it by position, and no element is a field of a returned mapping.
outputs.shape: As described in output mapping or tuple.
outputs.constraints: Tuple of finite derivative and optional theoretical frequencies; no hidden state.

preconditions: vv is a finite one-dimensional real array.
k is finite and positive; Fn, kappa and cutoff_mode select a supported branch.
supported: Fn=1,2,3 and Fn=4 with weak or smooth cutoff derivative.
Fn=3 point values of the triangle derivative, including the documented zero convention at v=-1,0,1 and outside [-1,1].
excluded: This leaf returns a derivative and optional theory frequencies; it does not evolve a state.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for unsupported Fn/cutoff_mode, nonfinite or non-vector vv, invalid kappa, invalid k or a non-increasing/nonuniform weak-cutoff grid.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError when the derivative is not finite.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative solve is performed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No mapping is returned after an exception.

example.code:
from scirel.kinetic.vlasov_poisson import vp_distribution
import numpy as np
g,wr,wi=vp_distribution(np.linspace(-6,6,101),4)
assert g.shape == (101,)
example.description: Evaluate the Fn=4 weak cutoff derivative on a 101-point velocity grid.
example.expected: PASS: .venv/bin/python completed; g has shape (101,) and the weak-cutoff branch is finite.

scope: Independent reference: the 40-digit mpmath definition of each built-in family decides the returned derivative. The Maxwellian has unit mass and unit variance, the kappa family's normalization follows the Beta integral B(1/2, kappa-1/2) and its variance the exact identity kappa Gamma(kappa-3/2)/Gamma(kappa-1/2) = 2 kappa/(2 kappa-3), the triangle's piecewise values are the classical open-interval ones, and the slowing-down derivative carries zero distributional mass. No SciPy special function and no implementation fixture is on the reference path.

Implementation relation: the four branches return -v exp(-v^2/2)/sqrt(2 pi), -c v (1+v^2/(2 kappa))^(-kappa-1) with c = Gamma(kappa)/(Gamma(kappa-1/2) sqrt(2 pi kappa)), the piecewise +1/-1/0 with 0 at the kinks v in {-1, 0, 1}, and -sign(v) 3 v^2 A/(|v|^3+vt^3)^2 with vt^2 = 2 halved at |v| = 4 plus the two weak-cutoff jump deposits of mass -+A/(64+vt^3); theory frequencies are returned only for Fn = 2, kappa = 1.

Test matrix: odd symmetry and finiteness for all four selectors, exact values at the kink nodes, unit mass and declared variance per family at 40 digits, the node v = 0 where the derivative vanishes exactly, and five rejection channels - unsupported Fn, kappa <= 1/2, an unknown cutoff_mode, a non-vector argument and a non-representable derivative - each asserted with its own message.

Precision budget, declared before the comparison was run: 1e-38 relative for the analytic normalizations and moments (theta-substitution quadrature at 40 digits, which removes the algebraic tail), 1e-14 relative for the derivative against the 40-digit closed form, and 1e-17 absolute at the node where it vanishes identically.

Cannot establish: the reported (wr, wi) = (1, -sqrt(2) k) for the kappa = 1 Lorentzian is not reproduced by either independent route. The 40-digit meromorphic closed form integral F'(v)/(v-z) dv = 1/(z - i sqrt(2))^2 places the roots of the code's own dispersion condition at omega = +-1 + i sqrt(2) k under its exp(-i omega t) convention, and every semidiscrete grid tested up to nv = 4096 and vmax = 40 has a purely real spectrum. Recorded as T-2026-0600 for a human decision; this contract does not restate the reported pair as established.
